personality_one_liner: A cinematic, immersive viewing experience where the UI recedes into the shadows, leaving content and live indicators to shine through translucent glass.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing around core content; grids use strict mathematical spacing. UI must feel breathable and not clamped to the screen edges.

do's: Use glass for bottom sheet overlays showing EPG data over live video
Use frosted nav bars and bottom tabs so video hints through the UI
Pair blur with a >=75% surface opacity tint under text to guarantee readability
dont's: Never blur body content or dense EPG data cells
Avoid stacking more than 2 blurred surfaces simultaneously

screens.name: Live TV Player
screens.purpose: Immersive fullscreen video playback that recedes into the background when tapped to reveal glass navigation and quick channel surfing.

states.loading: Dark surface with a centered, ruby-colored sleek spinner.
states.empty: N/A for player (always plays last channel or default).
states.error: Cinematic dark screen with error message and 'Retry Source' button.

screens.layout: Fullscreen absolute video player. When interacted, overlay a top-to-bottom dark gradient scrim (Layer 1). At the bottom, display a glassmorphic sheet containing player controls and a horizontally scrolling mini channel list.

screens.name: EPG Timeline Grid
screens.purpose: Classic horizontal TV guide layout for scheduling and setting reminders.

states.loading: Skeleton grid with shimmering glass cells.
states.empty: Illustration of an empty cinema seat with 'No Guide Data Available'.

screens.layout: Sticky left column (72pt wide) for Channel Logos (real PNGs or initials on brandTertiary backgrounds). Scrollable right area (both X and Y axes) for time slots. A vertical 'brandPrimary' (#E11D48) line indicates the current time. Program cells are sized proportionally to duration, using surfaceSecondary with border 0.5pt.

screens.name: EPG Box Grid (4-across)
screens.purpose: A visually rich, fast-scrolling grid to see what's on right now across all channels.
screens.layout: Adaptive grid (2-col on phones, 4-col on large screens). Wrap with flexDirection: 'row', flexWrap: 'wrap', space-between. Each card shows the Channel Logo at the top left, current program title prominently in Geist 500, a live progress bar at the bottom, and 'Next:' metadata. Uses surfaceSecondary.

screens.name: Favorites & Search
screens.purpose: Manage pinned channels and search the EPG for specific programs or categories.

states.empty: Empty state illustration of a star with 'Pin your favorite channels here'.

screens.layout: Top search bar with surfaceTertiary background. Below, a filtered list or grid of channels. When searching, split results into 'Channels' and 'Upcoming Programs' with clear section headers in Fraunces display font.

channel_placeholder.alt: Smart TV streaming placeholder for channel logo fallback

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Glass/Luxe guidelines: The app must feel like a premium smart TV experience adapted for mobile.

EPG Box Grid: Although the brief mentions '4-across', on portrait mobile phones, adapt this to a 2-col wrap grid (width: (screenWidth - 2*padding - gap) / 2) to maintain touch targets, but use 4-across if device is tablet/landscape. Document the responsiveness.
Text over video/images: ALWAYS use a gradient to dark scrim layer under text elements in the player overlay to ensure WCAG readability. text should use onSurfaceInverse.
For channel logos: Use the provided placeholder image OR use initials inside a brandTertiary circle when actual logos are missing. In real production, these come from the XMLTV feed.

EPG Timeline: The timeline grid requires both horizontal and vertical scrolling. Keep the channel column sticky on the left. The current time indicator should be a bold, brandPrimary (#E11D48) vertical line slicing through the grid.
Haptics: Add subtle haptic feedback when tapping channel rows, switching tabs, and setting reminders.
Typography: Use Fraunces for large section headers ('Live', 'TV Guide', 'Favorites') and Geist for dense UI components to maximize readability at small scale.
